record.title: Preprint reports safety-framed review attacks that steer AI-agent recommendations
record.summary: A 3 November 2026 preprint reports that fabricated safety warnings presented as ordinary consumer reviews can steer AI-agent recommendations without containing instructions to the model. Across six tested models and ten consumer-travel domains, the authors report 60.4% success for safety-framed reviews versus 66.0% for command-style injection; the former passed two evaluated injection detectors more often in their setup. The paper also reports transfer to four browser agents tested on one live review page and a corroboration instruction that reduced success in a non-adaptive test. These are author-reported findings, not estimates of deployed attack prevalence. Independent reproduction, adaptive attackers, genuine-warning trade-offs and broader transfer remain open.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors submitted arXiv:2611.04393v1 on 3 November 2026 at 06:26:58 UTC, reporting a study of safety-framed review attacks on AI-agent recommendations.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across six models and ten consumer-service domains, the authors report that fabricated safety warnings presented as ordinary reviews steered recommendations at 60.4%, compared with 66.0% for instruction-injection attacks, and passed more often through two evaluated injection detectors; the authors attribute the difference behind the filters to detector pass rates.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report transfer to four browser agents tested 20 times per attack on one live review page, and to a retrieval pipeline whose end-to-end success varied by retriever and exposure.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In a matched test on three models, the authors report that requiring independent corroboration before eliminating a provider on safety grounds reduced attack success from 68.4% to 3.6% against a non-adaptive attacker.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish attack prevalence in deployed systems, transfer beyond its consumer-travel recommendation setting, robustness to attackers who manufacture corroboration, or the operational cost of delaying action on genuine single-source safety warnings. No independent reproduction was inspected.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction or public access to the full payload set, review corpora or harness was found; the authors state these materials are embargoed and available by request under research-use terms.
The corroboration defense was evaluated against a non-adaptive attacker; adaptive corroboration and attacker coordination remain untested.
The safety-framed attack and defense are studied in single-turn consumer travel recommendations; delay on genuine hazards and transfer to other decisions are unknown.

brief.importance_rationale: If safety-framed evidence can steer deployed agents past command-focused defenses, it could materially change agent-security evaluation and design choices. The paper reports bounded tests; it does not establish prevalence, broad transfer or adaptive-defense robustness.
limitations: The empirical outcome claims are author-reported; no independent reproduction was inspected.
Controlled experiments use six models, ten consumer-service domains and single-turn recommendations based on fabricated reviews.
The browser transfer uses one live review page and 20 trials per attack for each of four agents; it does not estimate population risk.
Retrieval success varies with whether poisoned pages are retrieved.
The corroboration defense is tested against a non-adaptive attacker, and may delay action on a genuine hazard reported by only one source.
The authors state complete payloads and corpora are embargoed/request-only; public reproducibility is limited.
brief.summary: A 3 November 2026 preprint reports that fabricated safety warnings presented as ordinary consumer reviews can steer AI-agent recommendations without containing instructions to the model. Across six tested models and ten consumer-travel domains, the authors report 60.4% success for safety-framed reviews versus 66.0% for command-style injection; the former passed two evaluated injection detectors more often in their setup. The paper also reports transfer to four browser agents tested on one live review page and a corroboration instruction that reduced success in a non-adaptive test. These are author-reported findings, not estimates of deployed attack prevalence. Independent reproduction, adaptive attackers, genuine-warning trade-offs and broader transfer remain open.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report 60.4% attack success for safety-framed reviews versus 66.0% for instruction injection across the tested models/domains; after the two evaluated detector filters, safety-framed attacks were more effective in their test.
technical.demonstrated_result: The preprint, its date and reported experimental design are publicly inspectable. Empirical results remain author-reported; this review did not independently rerun them.
technical.implementation_status: Published preprint. Authors say full payloads, corpora and harness are embargoed/request-only; no independently runnable artifact was inspected.
technical.mechanism: An ordinary review asserts a safety hazard; the agent may eliminate legitimate providers on that evidence and thereby select an attacker-controlled listing. The text does not issue a command to the model.
technical.regime: Six models and ten consumer-service domains in controlled single-turn travel recommendations; browser transfer used one attacker-hosted page with four agents and 20 trials per attack; the retrieval study used a bounded set of review pages.
technical.reproducibility: The full paper and defense instruction are inspectable, but authors state payloads and corpora are embargoed/request-only. No independent reproduction was found.
technical.strongest_baseline: Matched conditions compare safety-framed reviews with command-style injection, misconduct complaints, benign-positive reviews and no-poison cases; the defense compares the same setup with and without a corroboration instruction against a non-adaptive attacker.

brief.title: Preprint reports safety-framed review attacks that steer AI-agent recommendations
brief.why_it_matters: If agents treat unverified safety claims in retrieved content as decisive, an attacker may steer consequential recommendations without using command-like prompt injection. The reported mechanism could change how retrieval and safety defenses are evaluated, but the evidence remains limited to the paper’s settings and has not been independently reproduced.
